ideas.title: Close the year with a look-back
ideas.desc: Pick the moments your fans reacted to most and replay them in one post. It is cheap to make and it ties the year together.
steps: List the 8-10 best moments of the year with the media team.
Cut them into one reel or carousel, newest to oldest or the reverse.
Schedule it for the last week of December and thank fans in the caption.
ideas.why: Hypothesis: a look-back lets fans relive moments they already liked, so it may be easy to share at the end of the year.

ideas.title: Turn the festive fixtures into a matchday poster
ideas.desc: A busy holiday schedule is the best moment for a clear graphic: who plays, when, and where to watch.
steps: Collect every match between Christmas and New Year with date and kick-off time.
Use one template with the same grid and colours for every poster.
Post it the morning of each match and update it in Stories.
hooks: [N] matches in [N] days. Here is the plan.
ideas.why: Hypothesis: a consistent matchday poster becomes a daily habit for fans during a busy fixture run.

ideas.title: Let a player front your sponsor's gift moment
ideas.desc: Pair one player with one product for a short, natural video. The gift feels like part of the club world, not an ad.
steps: Pick one player and one gift-friendly product from a sponsor.
Film a short, relaxed clip: the player reacts, tries or chooses.
Tag the sponsor and add a single link or action in the caption.
hooks: [Player] picked his favourite. Which is yours?
ideas.why: Hypothesis: a player using the product feels more natural than a product shot, and sponsors get a clear, shareable asset.

ideas.title: Film the arrival before the big game
ideas.desc: The walk into the stadium, the outfit, the greetings. A 15-second clip shows fans the day starting.
steps: Ask one media team member to wait at the entrance or the airport.
Capture 2-3 players arriving, no voice-over, just the sound.
Post it 2-3 hours before kick-off or the first session.
ideas.why: Hypothesis: arrival clips show the day starting, so fans may feel closer to the team before the game.

ideas.title: Fill quiet days with a sport swap
ideas.desc: When there is no match, let players try another sport. A visit to a rugby club or a golf challenge keeps the feed active.
steps: Choose a sport that fits your area, such as golf, padel or rugby.
Invite a local club or athlete to host your players for an hour.
Turn it into a challenge: who hits the best shot, who learns fastest?
hooks: We tried [sport]. It did not go as planned.
ideas.why: Hypothesis: a different sport with familiar faces may catch the attention of people who do not follow your team daily.

ideas.title: Prepare the champions post before the final
ideas.desc: Finals are decided in a minute. Have two versions of the post ready so you publish the right one in seconds.
steps: Draft one post for a win and one for a loss, with photo, line and graphic.
Agree who publishes and who approves, and test the flow.
Publish within minutes of the final whistle and reply to the first comments.
ideas.why: Hypothesis: speed matters in the first minutes after a title, so a prepared template may help you reach fans while emotion is high.
